From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@redpinebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident summary & customer action playbook

Tom — per our commitment, please find below a concise, customer-friendly post-incident summary, the event timeline, and the concrete actions we are taking. Full artifact bundle attached (timeline PDF, action ledger CSV, verification scripts).

Executive summary (2 lines):
- On Oct 13 between 19:45–20:40 PDT, Redwood experienced a transient capacity loss affecting a subset of hosted inference pools in us-west-2; this led to slower token throughput and, for some requests, an automated fallback to a lower-precision model variant which produced measurable drift for a narrow set of embeddings/scoring inputs.
- Impact to RedPine: delayed nightly scoring jobs (approx +180% runtime for some batches) and a small increase in false positives for two fraud models that use dense embeddings. No persistent data loss.

Root cause (summary):
- A race condition in our autoscaler’s drain logic could trigger concurrent eviction of GPU workers when multiple scaling events happen close together.
- During the eviction window, some requests were redirected to pools running a temporary quantized model variant (used as a compatibility fallback) which has different numeric characteristics — this introduced the model drift observed.
- KV-cache eviction metrics were also not surfaced quickly enough, increasing cold-starts for long-running prompts and amplifying latency.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-10-13 19:42 PDT: Autoscaler receives concurrent scale-down + maintenance signals following a transient network blip.
- 19:45–19:59 PDT: Multiple worker nodes drained in quick succession; request routing fell back to spare pools.
- 19:59–20:12 PDT: Several requests routed to quantized fallback model variant; customers with large batch scoring saw throughput degradation and some scoring variance.
- 20:12–20:40 PDT: Routing stabilizes after emergency autoscaler rollback and manual re-balancing; KV cache warm-up completed around 20:30.
- 20:50 PDT: All pools returned to normal capacity and routing policy.

Actions completed (what we did immediately):
- Emergency rollback of the autoscaler change set at 20:05 PDT to stop concurrent drains.
- Siloed the most affected pools and rebalanced traffic to healthy capacity.
- Snapshot logs and consumer metrics shared with your ops team (we received your log snippets; thank you).

Planned corrective measures (owners + ETA):
1) Autoscaler drain logic patch (prevents concurrent node eviction) — Owner: Jonas Weber — ETA: 2026-10-18 (deployed to staging), 2026-10-21 (prod rollout behind canary).
2) Stronger fallback policy: disallow automatic fallback to quantized variants for customers with pinned model profiles; instead use queued retries + rate-limited spillover — Owner: Marissa Cole — ETA: 2026-10-20 (policy change), 2026-10-25 (completed rollout).
3) KV-cache telemetry: expose real-time eviction/heat metrics and an alert for cache cold-start spikes — Owner: Platform Observability — ETA: 2026-10-19 (initial dashboards), 2026-10-26 (alerts).
4) Regression tests: add an integration test that replays RedPine’s scoring workload to confirm no precision drift under failover scenarios — Owner: Reliability Eng (Jonas) — ETA: 2026-10-22.
5) Customer verification playbook: step-by-step checks (endpoints to hit, expected percentile latency and embedding-difference thresholds) and a reproducible test harness — Owner: Customer Reliability (Sofia) — ETA: 2026-10-16 (deliverable attached).

Compensation and next steps:
- We will apply a two-week credit to RedPine’s account for the period covering Oct 13 disruption; Marissa will confirm the credit details and timing.
- We’d like to schedule a 30-min verification call the week of Oct 19 to run the verification playbook together; proposed slots attached in the calendar invite.
- Please confirm whether you want the autoscaler patch rolled to prod behind a slow canary (recommended) or accelerated (we can support an expedited path subject to your signoff).

Attachments (attached to this email):
- redwood-incident-timeline-20261014.pdf (detailed timeline + logs index)
- mitigation-action-ledger-20261014.csv (action owner, ETA, status)
- verification-scripts.md (how RedPine can run independent checks + sample outputs)

If helpful, we can also provide a small set of raw traces around the event window for your SRE team — Elena from DataSec is copied here in case you want vendor forensic support.

We take this seriously and are committed to preventing recurrence. I’ll post status updates to the ticket (INF-482) and follow up once the autoscaler patch passes staging validation.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Lead, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
